title: Design System: World Travel Photobook Atlas

extensions.tonalRampNote: Tonal ramps are panel metadata synthesized for inspection; they are not additional implemented palette tokens.

title.purpose: Chinese album title projected onto the curved glass; bundled Manrope is the closest available reference match.

body.purpose: Smaller English title on the same curved surface.

label.purpose: Quiet bottom-centred desktop and mobile interaction guidance.

editorial-title.purpose: Widely spaced serif annotation over the photograph's negative space.

editorial-caption.purpose: Compact serif place annotation; the approximate-area line is separately italic.

reader-title.purpose: The selected original album's title in the preserved warm reading header.

shadows.name: player-ambient
shadows.purpose: Continuous player shell only; never individual content strips.

shadows.name: player-focus
shadows.purpose: Visible keyboard focus on the continuous glass shell.

shadows.name: photograph-lift
shadows.purpose: Lifts the unfiltered photographic projection above deep space.

motion.name: hand-opening
motion.purpose: Black, fist, unfurling palm, geographic Earth and satellites, followed by the hand leaving.

motion.name: book-journey
motion.purpose: Live departure, space, atmosphere, clouds, destination, materialization and book opening.

motion.name: reduced-journey
motion.purpose: Short reading transition when reduced motion is requested; the hand sequence and ambient motion are skipped.

motion.name: preview-release
motion.purpose: Brief release delay before resuming the album orbit after the pointer or focus leaves.

motion.name: player-rim-state
motion.purpose: Glass surface opacity response to active state.

materials.playerGlass: backdrop-filter: blur(5px) saturate(.82); one continuous SVG rim and 31 borderless projected content strips
materials.playerRim: linear gradient from #c7e1f1 through #fff5dc and #edcda9 to #e8d3f7; 1.3px normal, 1.8px active/focus
materials.sky: NASA/Goddard SVS 8K star catalogue image; opacity .27 in planet mode and .36 in album mode
materials.mapFootprint: Transparent real-data layers occupy negative space within 15–25%; current ten SVG metadata values are 18.7–23.5%
materials.book: Native perspective hardcover, visible page-edge blocks and four principal curved folios

components.name: Atlas mode switch
components.description: Upper-right control between small planets and the album orbit.

components.name: Opening replay
components.description: Quiet upper-left pill that replays the four-second hand and Earth opening.

narrative.overview:
A miniature geographic Earth is the centre of this world. A human hand introduces its scale, while a broad, softly turbulent cyan and indigo nebula gives the surrounding space volume. Continents, oceans, clouds and city lights remain legible throughout the opening and album modes. The background is almost black, with a restrained NASA star catalogue image rather than a dense field of decorative particles.

Albums float as transparent, bowed players around Earth. Their warm ivory lettering and fine controls feel delicate against the cold space. Hovering reveals an editorial photograph with a small transparent geographic layer; entering an album carries that same destination into a golden flight and a tangible, opening book. The photographs and existing readers remain the content authority.
keyCharacteristics: Geographic Earth, human scale and spacious deep black.
Soft cyan nebula volume with sparse, distant stars.
Three orbital tiers of continuously curved, warm glass players.
Unfiltered photography with restrained real geography and serif annotation.
Live cinematic transitions into the selected original photobook.

rules.name: The Light Has a Place Rule
rules.body: Cyan belongs to the surrounding atmosphere and nebula; the central body remains geographic Earth in every scene mode.

rules.name: The Surface Carries Type Rule
rules.body: Player titles, progress lines and controls bend with the glass surface; text must not float on an independent flat rectangle.

rules.name: The Single Rim Rule
rules.body: The player has one uninterrupted glass boundary. Its projected content strips have no individual borders, fills or shadows.

dos: Do keep geographic Earth visible as Earth throughout the hand opening and album modes.
Do use one soft, irregular cyan and indigo nebula volume with restrained star brightness.
Do bend the entire player surface, including its type and progress line, inside one continuous rim.
Do preserve photograph colour, aspect ratio and original reader content.
Do keep real geographic overlays in negative space within the confirmed 15–25% footprint and label approximate areas honestly.
Do preserve Escape, keyboard focus and the 220ms reduced-motion journey alternative.
donts: Don't substitute a cratered moon, blue energy ball or central vortex for Earth.
Don't replace the nebula with parallel ellipse strokes or separate luminous rails.
Don't give each projected content strip its own glass border or treat the player symbols as independent working buttons.
Don't tint, blur or stretch the original photograph to create the editorial map treatment.
Don't claim the closest available font is identical to the reference font, or that a photographic destination plate is a true aerial approach.
